{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "feasible",
    "answerable": [
      "Elevation gradient of peak (annual maximum) SWE across the Wenatchee basin",
      "Model-vs-observed comparison of peak SWE and snow timing at the 5 SNOTEL locations",
      "Interannual variability of peak SWE (1980-2018) at each elevation band"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "Spatially distributed/basin-wide SWE fields (no dense snow courses available for validation)",
      "Attribution of biases to specific drivers other than elevation (only elevation provided as candidate driver)"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 5,
  "n_justification": "One single-column site is placed at each of the 5 SNOTEL stations so that simulated peak SWE can be directly compared to observations and the elevation gradient (low to high) can be resolved with matched validation data.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "fish_lake_1036m", "lat": 47.5556, "lon": -120.7175, "soil_texture": "loam"},
    {"id": "trinity_1128m", "lat": 47.9036, "lon": -120.9142, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "stevens_pass_1238m", "lat": 47.7442, "lon": -121.0894, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "tunnel_ave_1173m", "lat": 47.7000, "lon": -121.0333, "soil_texture": "loam"},
    {"id": "miners_ridge_1856m", "lat": 47.9825, "lon": -120.9550, "soil_texture": "gravelly_sandy_loam"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1980",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2018",
    "STOP_N": "39",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "1980-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "H2OSNO",
      "SNOWDP",
      "SNOW",
      "RAIN",
      "QSNOMELT",
      "QFLX_SNOW_GRND",
      "FSNO",
      "SNOWICE",
      "SNOWLIQ",
      "TSA",
      "TBOT",
      "FSDS",
      "FLDS",
      "TG",
      "TSOI"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "single_point_ELM",
    "SNOTEL_SWE_observations",
    "GSWP3_or_equivalent_atmospheric_forcing_1980_2018",
    "surface_dataset_generation_per_site"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "STOP_OPTION=nyears with a preceding multi-year accumulated spin-up to equilibrate soil/snow states before the 1980-2018 analysis period",
    "Column elevations follow SNOTEL station metadata; forcing is lapse-rate corrected or elevation-adjusted to each site to represent the gradient",
    "Peak SWE is defined as the annual maximum of daily/monthly H2OSNO per water year",
    "Coordinates and elevations approximate the 5 Wenatchee-basin SNOTEL stations (Fish Lake, Trinity, Stevens Pass, Tunnel Ave, Miners Ridge); exact station IDs/coords should be confirmed against NRCS metadata",
    "Land-cover set to evergreen needleleaf forest / montane vegetation typical of the basin at each site",
    "Model output daily where possible to resolve snow accumulation/melt timing for comparison"

answerable: Elevation gradient of peak (annual maximum) SWE across the Wenatchee basin
Model-vs-observed comparison of peak SWE and snow timing at the 5 SNOTEL locations
Interannual variability of peak SWE (1980-2018) at each elevation band
not_answerable: Spatially distributed/basin-wide SWE fields (no dense snow courses available for validation)
Attribution of biases to specific drivers other than elevation (only elevation provided as candidate driver)

parsed.n_justification: One single-column site is placed at each of the 5 SNOTEL stations so that simulated peak SWE can be directly compared to observations and the elevation gradient (low to high) can be resolved with matched validation data.
assumptions: STOP_OPTION=nyears with a preceding multi-year accumulated spin-up to equilibrate soil/snow states before the 1980-2018 analysis period
Column elevations follow SNOTEL station metadata; forcing is lapse-rate corrected or elevation-adjusted to each site to represent the gradient
Peak SWE is defined as the annual maximum of daily/monthly H2OSNO per water year

Coordinates and elevations approximate the 5 Wenatchee-basin SNOTEL stations (Fish Lake, Trinity, Stevens Pass, Tunnel Ave, Miners Ridge); exact station IDs/coords should be confirmed against NRCS metadata
Land-cover set to evergreen needleleaf forest / montane vegetation typical of the basin at each site
Model output daily where possible to resolve snow accumulation/melt timing for comparison
